parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no documented facility ban, no documented police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, no documented trans violence data, and no sourced border/visa rule singling out trans travellers. The struck sodomy provisions are decriminalised and tangential anyway. What depresses the score is recourse and climate, not a documented exposure: no anti-discrimination or hate-speech protection in accommodation, transport or employment, so a refused or harassed visitor has no statutory remedy; civil society reports LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement, so police are an unreliable route after assault; and a 2005 port refusal of an LGBTQ cruise ship, though dated and ad hoc, shows official willingness to exclude. No LGR, no union recognition are resident-facing and weighted lightly. Open questions (border screening, custody/ward placement) are unanswered, not exposures. Sits below the 0.55–0.65 tier, which shows working remedies or documented acceptance; above the 0.35–0.45 tier, which shows a current universal institutional exclusion.
